**Finding: deviation (§ 2.2, p0013).**

The minimum-commitment provisions are otherwise strongly in our favour and sit at the preferred position:
- § 2.1 — "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies," and declining a further Order Form "is not a breach or shortfall."
- § 7.1 — Vendor may not impose unstated minimum-use charges.
- § 12.3 — Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.
- § 22.2–22.3 "shortfall" references are audit true-ups on usage, not take-or-pay penalties.

The problem hides in the exclusivity provision the planner flagged: § 2.2 makes Vendor our **sole and exclusive provider** of hosted analytics services for the entire term. That is a full-requirements commitment on us with no reduction or termination right, so it fails the fallback (no 12-month limit, no 30 days' notice reduction, no true-up), and it directly contradicts § 12.3.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: § 2.2 becomes a non-exclusive appointment, with confirmation that we owe nothing absent an Order Form.
